content: 1. Cobicistat and CYP3A4 Substrates: Cobicistat is a potent inhibitor of the CYP3A4 enzyme. It is contraindicated with drugs that are metabolized by CYP3A4 and for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious or life-threatening events. Close monitoring is required when co-administering such drugs. 2. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Ethosuximide: This combination increases ethosuximide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 3. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Etodolac: Co-administration may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 4. Emtricitabine and Tenofovir with NSAIDs: Co-administration with high-dose or multiple-dose NSAIDs can increase the risk of nephrotoxicity due to shared excretion pathways (glomerular filtration and tubular secretion). Alternatives to NSAIDs should be considered, and patients should be closely monitored. 5. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Etoposide: This combination increases etoposide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. 6. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Etravirine: Etravirine decreases the levels of this combination by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated, and alternative therapies should be used. 7. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Exemestane: This combination increases exemestane levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 8. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Felbamate: This combination increases felbamate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 9. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Felodipine: This combination increases felodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 10. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Fenofibrate: This combination increases fenofibrate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 11. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Fenoprofen: Co-administration may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 12. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Fexinidazole: Fexinidazole inhibits CYP3A4 and may increase the levels of this combination, leading to adverse effects. This interaction is contraindicated, and alternative therapies should be used. 13. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Fineranone: This combination increases fineranone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 14. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Flecainide: This combination increases flecainide levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 15. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Flibanserin: Co-administration with flibanserin is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope when combined with CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Fluoxetine: This combination increases fluoxetine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 17. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Fluphenazine: This combination increases fluphenazine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 18. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Flurazepam: This combination increases flurazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Benzodiazepine dose reduction should be considered, and patients should be closely monitored. 19. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Flutamide: This combination increases flutamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 20. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Fluticasone: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure to fluticasone, leading to adverse effects. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 21. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Fluvastatin: This combination decreases fluvastatin levels by inducing CYP2C9 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 22. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Fluvoxamine: This combination increases fluvoxamine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be closely monitored. 23. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin decreases the levels of this combination by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 24. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Futibatinib: Co-administration with futibatinib and strong CYP3A inhibitors may increase the risk of futibatinib toxicities. Alternative therapies should be considered. 25. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Ganaxolone: Changes in ganaxolone exposure are not expected to be clinically significant when co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitoring is recommended. 26. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Ganciclovir: Co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 27. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Gefitinib: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended. 28. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Gentamicin: Co-administration may increase nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 29. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Geprione: This combination increases geprione levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is contraindicated. 30. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Glimepiride/Glipizide/Glyburide: This combination decreases the levels of these drugs by inducing CYP2C9 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 31. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Guanfacine: Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors significantly increase guanfacine plasma concentrations. Dosage adjustments are recommended, particularly for extended-release formulations. 32. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Haloperidol: This combination increases haloperidol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 33. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Hydrocodone: Co-administration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Alternative therapies should be considered. 34. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Ibrutinib: Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. If short-term use of a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is necessary, interrupt ibrutinib therapy. 35. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Ibuprofen: Co-administration may increase toxicity by reducing renal clearance. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are recommended.
